# Native Wrapped-Path Closure

This provisional F07 calculation records the opt-in source closure for native
OpenSim muscle paths that use wrapping geometry. It establishes a narrow
software-admission and native-observation contract. It does not establish
anatomical correctness, physiological plausibility, path worklessness, guide
work bounds, contact or grip, or an accepted full-capture endpoint. Publication
remains blocked.

## Exact Source Declaration

For a model byte sequence $B$, the source identity is
$h_s = \operatorname{SHA256}(B)$. The declaration binds $h_s$ and an ordered,
duplicate-free inventory of supported native components. Each wrap object
records its absolute component path, concrete type, parent frame, translation,
body-fixed XYZ rotation, active flag, quadrant, dimensions, and hash of its
native component serialization. The current shape profile is limited to
`WrapCylinder`, `WrapEllipsoid`, and `WrapSphere`.

Each `PathWrap` records its absolute path and owner, exact target path and name,
method, range, and component serialization hash. Its target must be one of the
declared wrap objects. The current method profile is `hybrid`; the range is
either the native `(-1, -1)` sentinel or an ordered pair of nonnegative integer
indices. Each `ConditionalPathPoint` records its owner, exact coordinate path,
strictly increasing active range, and component serialization hash. All
floating-point geometry and range values must be finite. These checks close
the named source declarations; they do not prove the target geometry is
anatomically correct.

Before constrained replay, the native model is reloaded and its complete
declaration is compared to the caller's source-bound declaration. Any source
hash change, unsupported shape or method, unresolved target, mismatched target
name/path, or changed component serialization blocks execution. In the default
path, wrapped components remain rejected unless the caller explicitly supplies
the typed declaration. The declaration hash is retained in the replay
admission identity so it cannot be silently substituted on replay.

## Native Route Observation

When a reference state is supplied, the audit reuses the maintained native
reference observer to report the actual evaluated route and conditional-point
state. The observation is tied to the same source hash and does not alter the
source, repair a route, or extrapolate beyond sampled states. A route observed
at one state does not prove global path smoothness or worklessness over a full
coordinate chart. Missing global route-transition and guide-work evidence is
an unqualified diagnostic finding requiring the shared explicit diagnostic
opt-in in Chapter 56; it does not authorize a physiological claim.

Nonfinite geometry, an inconsistent native path, or a failed source closure is
an execution blocker. Unqualified work or transition evidence is recorded
separately from execution viability. This profile does not admit nonlinear
`MovingPathPoint` laws, generalized `CustomJoint` functions, contact forces, or
other unreviewed components; their complete typed native source closure remains
a separate dependency.

## Native Fixture Evidence and Limits

`tests/opensim/test_native_wrapped_path.py` exercises actual OpenSim 4.6 native
wrapping for cylinders, ellipsoids, and spheres; verifies source-hash and
PathWrap-link mutation rejection; observes a conditional path point on both
sides of its declared range; verifies default rejection; and performs an
opt-in constrained replay. These fixtures establish implementation behavior
for the declared synthetic cases only. They do not validate external model
resources, the frozen full-body capture, global route work budgets, or human
muscle limits.

The shared diagnostic contract in Chapter 56 is a dependency for runner-level
request serialization and finding aggregation. Until that dependency is
integrated and the governed checks pass, this chapter remains provisional and
the calculation inventory is not promoted.
